claim: HHNI supports multi-level (six) hierarchy for retrieval.
Implementation artifacts exist and pass tests.
Two-stage retrieval (coarse->refine) increases precision while preserving diversity.
Authority and time are first-class signals in hierarchical retrieval.
HHNI consists of five core components: Index Engine, DVNS Physics Module, Retrieval Planner, Compression/Deduplication Module, and IO/Adapters.
DVNS uses four physics forces: gravity (attraction), elastic (structure), repulse (separation), damping (stability).
HHNI achieves +15% RS-lift at precision-at-rank-5, empirically validated improvement over baseline.
Two-stage retrieval: Stage 1 (coarse) ~10ms latency, Stage 2 (physics) ~30-50ms latency, total p95 < 80ms.
HHNI integrates with CMC for atom indexing, APOE for context retrieval, VIF for witness storage, SEG for evidence indexing, SDF-CVF for index consistency.
Operational context replay runbook documents the five-step workflow before merges.
DVNS simulator module exposes gravity/elastic/repulse/damping forces used in production.
Gate policy enforces Tier S thresholds (vif_min, intelligent metrics) for HHNI.
Wave 1 sequencing and status logging live in READY_TO_EXECUTE.md and SHARED_MESSAGE_BOARD.md.
